setup: Sit or stand tall with an upright posture, shoulders relaxed down and back, looking straight ahead.
steps: Draw your chin directly backward horizontally, creating a slight double chin, without tilting your head down.
Hold the retracted position for the designated pause, feeling a gentle stretch at the base of the skull.
Slowly release back to the neutral starting position under control.
instructions.breathing: Breathe naturally and steadily throughout the hold; do not hold your breath.
cues: Slide your head straight back like closing a drawer
Make a double chin without looking down
Keep eyes level on the horizon

common_faults.fault: Flexing the neck downward rather than translating it backward
common_faults.correction: Keep your gaze parallel to the floor; move straight back along a horizontal track.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward during retraction
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulders relaxed and down away from your ears.

precautions: Avoid forcing movement into pain or tingling sensations down the neck or arms.

name: Chin Tuck
summary: A postural rehabilitation exercise that retracts the head to strengthen deep cervical flexors and lengthen tight upper neck extensors.
